title: Deterministic Predicate Processor for Structured Neuropsychological Modeling Based on Multi-Level Nested Dictionaries and Inflectional Regular Expression Analysis
content: Formalizing the transition from qualitative, phenomenological neuropsychological observations to quantitative clinical data structures remains a critical bottleneck in computational neuroscience. Existing methods either rely on scalar psychometric screening tools (e.g., MoCA, MMSE) that obscure the modular and network-level topography of cognitive deficits, or utilize stochastic large language models (LLMs) prone to diagnostic hallucination and predicate drift. This paper presents a deterministic expert core architecture that bridges network neuroscience and clinical practice by formalizing A.R. Luria’s theory of systemic-dynamic localization of higher mental functions into a production-rule predicate processor. The system converts an input 10-dimensional integer vector of multi-domain cognitive error scores [0-5] into standardized syndromic profiles using multi-level nested dictionary traversals and automated mapping onto the WHO International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) taxonomy (b, d, and e codes). To ensure morphosyntactic invariance across language localizations, an isolated regular expression inflection module handles gender agreement tags post-traversal. The computational runtime maintains strict algorithmic transparency, enforces cross-domain data integrity filters, and implements a deterministic interrupt for vector singularities, eliminating probabilistic inference and ensuring auditable, reproducible clinical decision-support reporting.
